task_name: the order of the ranking and the use case that answers it

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each is in the diff. 'rank every clone of the root by line coverage': CoverageRanking.run() asks the catalog for the clones (`await this.deps.catalog.list()`), reads each one through the port in parallel with Promise.all, and hands the entries to CoverageOrder.sort, which orders the measured by `other.reading.lines.percentage() - one.reading.lines.percentage()`. 'with the clones that have no percentage last': rankOf gives 'measured' 0 and both 'no-artifact' and 'unreadable-artifact' 1, and rankDiff is applied before any percentage comparison. 'an unreadable artefact reported instead of sinking the ranking': CoverageRanking.readingOf catches UnreadableArtifact and returns `{ id: clone.id, reading: CoverageReadings.unreadableArtifact() }`, so that clone stays as an entry with a state instead of failing the run; any other error is rethrown, which is not sinking the ranking but refusing to hide an unrelated fault.

The TDD line names `test('two clones with the same percentage are ordered by name')`; it is in the diff and its body is what the sentence asks for. It measures beta and alpha at exactly the same percentage (500/1000 both) and asserts `expect(entries.map((entry) => entry.id)).toEqual(['alpha', 'beta'])` over a catalog that hands them out in the opposite order ([beta, alpha]), so the name is what decides. The double is the one the line describes: CoverageArtifactsDouble.readingOf answers by the path it is asked for (`this.answers.get(repoPath)`) and raises for a path nobody wrote an answer for (`throw new Error('no answer configured for ' + repoPath)`). The second boundary case the line demands is also there: in 'the ranking puts the higher percentage first' zeta is 501/1000 and alpha 500/1000 — 0.1 apart, with the name order the opposite one (alpha < zeta) — and the assertion expects ['zeta', 'alpha'], so a sort that ignored the percentage would fail.

Symbol by symbol against the two Contract blocks. coverage-order.ts: `export class CoverageOrder` with `sort(entries: readonly RepoCoverage[]): RepoCoverage[]` — same name, same parameter name and type, same return type; sort does not mutate its input (`[...entries].sort(...)`), consistent with the readonly parameter. coverage-ranking.ts: `export interface RankedCoverage { entries: readonly RepoCoverage[] }` — identical; `export class CoverageRanking` with `constructor(deps: { catalog: Catalog; artifacts: CoverageArtifacts; order: CoverageOrder })` — same single named object, same three member names and types, and `run(): Promise<RankedCoverage>` — identical. The types it leans on match the ones already committed: Catalog in server/src/repos.ts declares `list(): Promise<Clone[]>` and `resolve(id: string): Promise<string | null>`; CoverageArtifacts declares `readingOf(repoPath: string): Promise<CoverageReading>`; RepoCoverage is `{ id: string; reading: CoverageReading }`; CoverageState is the three-member union CoverageOrder.rankOf dispatches over; CoverageReadings.unreadableArtifact() and UnreadableArtifact are used with the shapes those modules export. No call site the brief names for this task.

Row by row, only the rows this diff bears on. 'Order of the ranking — measured first by percentage descending, then every non-measured; ties broken by id ascending, compared by code unit': implemented exactly — rankOf ranks measured 0 and both non-measured states 1, the percentage compares descending, and byId compares with `one < other ? -1 : 1`, no localeCompare. 'Artefact that is not its format — the reader raises UnreadableArtifact, the use case turns it into state unreadable-artifact': implemented in CoverageRanking.readingOf, in the use case and not in an adapter. 'No candidate counts — state no-artifact, every value null': respected through CoverageReadings.noArtifact(), which the diff only consumes. 'New server code lives under server/src/coverage/, one concept per module': three files under that directory, one concept each. 'Spanish is only for UI copy': every identifier, test name and diagnostic in the diff is English. Rows this diff does not touch (Route, Formats, Candidate order, Metric, artefact with no line counters, Measure date, Cache key) are not findings. No row is reopened.

Exemplars. server/src/repos.ts is the one that bears on this task and CoverageOrder.byId is its idiom transplanted: byName is `if (one.name === other.name) return 0; return one.name < other.name ? -1 : 1`, byId is the same three lines over id, so the answer does not move with LANG. CoverageRanking reads every clone with Promise.all, the same way Catalog.list builds its entries in parallel. server/src/api/routes.ts and web/* exemplars have no counterpart in this task (no route, no adapter, no UI here). Repo rules of AGENTS.md, the ones that bear: code in English — all identifiers and test names are; tests beside the code with Vitest — server/src/coverage/coverage-ranking.test.ts imports from 'vitest'; relative imports in server/ carry the .js suffix — all nine do ('./coverage-order.js', '../repos.js', ...); no author name or email leaves the server — RepoCoverage carries id and reading only; the server never mutates a clone and never fetches — this diff performs no I/O at all; web/ imports nothing from server/ — web/ is untouched. ct's five documents, which win rule by rule. architecture.md applies (three new modules, all marked (create)): CoverageOrder is the policy — the exact rule, immutable, no I/O, importing only type declarations of its own module tree, knowing nobody; it is total, dispatching over CoverageState in a switch with no catch-all branch, so a fourth member breaks the build instead of falling into a default; it returns the whole effect (an ordered array), not a boolean. CoverageRanking is the use case — dependencies enter through the constructor by name, they are the ports Catalog and CoverageArtifacts plus the domain policy, never an adapter; no suffix on the type; it declares its result object RankedCoverage beside itself even though it carries one field; it translates no external format and maps no keys by hand; the error-to-state mapping it does hold is the policy of what to do with one clone's failure, which the brief places here on purpose and which architecture.md keeps out of the adapter. One concept per module: order, use case, and the test beside them. style.md: no comment and no docstring in any of the three new files; every function hangs off a type (CoverageOrder, CoverageRanking, and in the test CloneMother, CatalogDouble, CoverageArtifactsDouble — no module-level function); English throughout. decisions.md: the ranking rule is written once, in CoverageOrder, and nothing else in the diff re-derives it; byId beside repos.ts byName is the idiom of a comparison, not a business decision that would force touching both at once, and the brief names repos.ts as the file to imitate for exactly that. testing.md: the clone is built by a mother (CloneMother.at) so each test names only what its case changes; the double answers by what it is asked and raises when nobody wrote an answer; values are real instances (LineCount.of, CoverageReadings) and none is doubled; the test is outside-in on the application layer with the ports doubled, and the domain policy is covered along that path with no test of its own; every test name is a sentence about what is guaranteed, not about a method. Read as the document asks — could each assertion fail for the reason its name gives — all five can: reverse the percentage comparison and test 1 falls, drop byId and test 2 falls, give the non-measured states rank 0 and tests 3 and 4 fall, remove the UnreadableArtifact catch and test 5 falls with the error. defects.md, its four rules named one by one. Closed vocabulary: the subject is CoverageState, held as a three-member union and dispatched over in rankOf with no catch-all and no boolean derived from it; the absent state is a member ('no-artifact'), not an optional — conforms. Raw map as the return value of logic: sort returns RepoCoverage[], run returns the declared RankedCoverage; the only Map in the diff is the double's private answers table, which is test scaffolding and not the return value of logic — conforms. Two fields that have to agree: CoverageReading is a discriminated union, so lines/source/measuredAt exist only in the measured arm; the diff introduces no flag beside them and no sentinel — no zero percentage standing for 'not measured', which is what the desired end state forbids — conforms. Error named for what happens, not for where: the only error the diff handles is UnreadableArtifact, named for what happened to the artefact, and the rethrow of anything else keeps that name meaningful; the diff declares no new error type — conforms. No clash between a control of the plan and any of these five documents: the module's own test count is what the Verification pins, not the suite total, so nothing forbade the assertions testing.md asks for. No skill was named in Rules to obey, so no skill had to be loaded for this item.

Does not apply: the diff has no `-` line at all. All three files are new (new file mode 100644, index 0000000), the package reports '3 files changed, 189 insertions(+)' and zero deletions, so there is no pre-existing assertion, case or test that could have been removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by the test's scaffolding. The ordering comes from CoverageOrder.compare in server/src/coverage/coverage-order.ts — rankOf for the measured/non-measured split, the percentage subtraction for the descending order, byId for the tie — and the reporting of an unreadable artefact comes from the catch in CoverageRanking.readingOf. The test's own pieces (CloneMother, CatalogDouble, CoverageArtifactsDouble) only supply inputs: the double answers a reading per clone path and raises UnreadableArtifact, and it never orders anything nor names a state in an answer that the assertion then reads back. Revert coverage-order.ts and coverage-ranking.ts and no expected order survives: entries would come out in catalog order and the unreadable clone would throw.

Inside the three declared files the diff writes only what the task asks for. coverage-order.ts holds CoverageOrder and nothing else — sort plus its three private helpers, all of them the rule the task describes. coverage-ranking.ts holds RankedCoverage and CoverageRanking, which the Contract block declares, plus the private readingOf that performs the UnreadableArtifact mapping the task assigns to the use case. The test file holds the five tests the Tests marker lists and the mother and two doubles they need. Nothing from 'Out of scope' appears: no test or coverage tool is run inside a clone, no CI or external service is read, no history or trend, no per-folder or per-file coverage, no threshold or colour, no JaCoCo. No route, no adapter, no cache, no reader of an artefact — the neighbouring tasks' work is absent. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix of an existing file: no existing file is touched.

The five new tests measured on the three properties that block. Deterministic: no assertion touches the clock, the network or a path — every assertion is on entry ids or on entry.reading.state; the `new Date()` inside the double's measured() answer feeds measuredAt, which no test reads, and the percentages come from fixed integer counts (501/1000, 500/1000), so the same code cannot pass today and fail tomorrow; no randomness, no sleep, no file. Isolated: each test builds its own CloneMother clones, its own CatalogDouble and its own CoverageArtifactsDouble whose answers Map is a private instance field, so nothing is shared, nothing is reset and no test needs the order of the file or state another test left. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what CoverageRanking returned after CoverageOrder sorted it, never on a mock's call count, a stub's return value or a constant the test defined — the double is asked for readings and the expected orders it never states. Nothing finer to report, so the finer half needed no citation and the TDD skill was not loaded.
